mission:
Implement CSV analytics export.
Plan this as a single implementation task for the export (with its tests). Generating and reading the contract is the first step of that task, not a task of its own.
Add src/export.js exporting `exportCsv(records)`, which returns CSV text for analytics records like the ones in src/records.js, with node:test tests in test/export.test.js.
The output must conform to the project export contract. The contract is generated: run `npm run generate-schema` and follow generated/export-contract.json exactly.
Follow docs/CONVENTIONS.md. `npm test` must pass.
hiddenPrerequisite: src/normalize.js (only named inside the packed contract)

planV1.summary: Add src/export.js exporting `exportCsv(records)` plus node:test tests in test/export.test.js, as one implementation task. The task's first step is running `npm run generate-schema` and reading generated/export-contract.json, which is binding (docs/CONVENTIONS.md line 5). The contract's contents are not known at planning time: generated/ does not exist in the checkout, vendor/export-contract.bundle is a packed binary, and the planner role is read-only so I did not run the generator. The plan therefore fixes no column, ordering, normalisation, quoting or line-ending rules; the worker must take them from the generated contract.

The contract can be satisfied with a single new module, src/export.js. If it requires another module (e.g. a shared normalisation helper), docs/CONVENTIONS.md line 6 forbids writing it inside this task; it must become its own task.

Input records have the shape shown in src/records.js (id, customer, amount, currency, timestamp), with messy values (padded whitespace, a combining character, string and numeric amounts, lower-case currency, non-UTC offset) that the contract presumably says how to normalise.
Bad input to exportCsv (e.g. a non-array, or whatever else the contract defines as invalid) throws TypeError, per docs/CONVENTIONS.md line 7.
generated/ and vendor/export-contract.bundle are not committed or edited (docs/CONVENTIONS.md line 4, vendor/README.md).

The output of `exportCsv` conforms to every rule in generated/export-contract.json as produced by `npm run generate-schema` (columns, order, header, delimiter, quoting, line endings, value normalisation, row ordering and any other rule it states).
test/export.test.js exists, uses node:test, and covers the contract rules including the SAMPLE records from src/records.js and TypeError on bad input.
`npm test` exits 0, with both test/records.test.js and test/export.test.js passing.
No files other than src/export.js and test/export.test.js are added or modified in git; generated/ stays untracked and vendor/ is untouched.

tasks.title: Implement exportCsv per the generated export contract, with tests
tasks.description:
Repository: analytics-kit, plain ESM JavaScript (package.json has "type": "module"), no dependencies, tests run with `npm test` (`node --test`). Platform is native Windows; use PowerShell-compatible commands.

Step 1 (mandatory, before writing any code): run `npm run generate-schema`. This runs scripts/generate-contract.mjs, which unpacks vendor/export-contract.bundle into generated/export-contract.json. Read that file in full. It is the binding export contract (docs/CONVENTIONS.md) and its contents were NOT available when this plan was written, so nothing here describes the CSV format: take columns, column order, header, delimiter, quoting/escaping, line endings, trailing newline, row ordering, value normalisation (whitespace, Unicode, numbers, currency, timestamps), empty-input behaviour and any other rule from the contract, and follow it exactly. Do not guess or fall back to generic CSV defaults where the contract is specific. If the generator fails or the contract is ambiguous or self-contradictory, report a blocker with the command output rather than inventing rules.

Step 2: create src/export.js exporting the named function `exportCsv(records)`, which returns the CSV text for an array of analytics records shaped like SAMPLE in src/records.js (fields id, customer, amount, currency, timestamp; note the sample deliberately contains padded/repeated whitespace in customer, a combining accent character, amount as both string and number, lower-case currency and a non-UTC timestamp offset). Errors thrown for bad input must be TypeError. Match the style of the existing code (no semicolons, single quotes, short comment at top of file).

Step 3: create test/export.test.js using node:test and node:assert/strict (same style as test/records.test.js). Derive expected values from the contract rules, not from whatever the implementation happens to output. Cover: the exact output for SAMPLE from src/records.js, each normalisation/quoting/ordering rule in the contract, empty input, and TypeError for bad input.

Step 4: run `npm test` and confirm it passes.

Constraints from docs/CONVENTIONS.md: create only src/export.js and test/export.test.js. If the contract turns out to require a module that this task does not name (for example a separate helper module mandated by the contract), do NOT write it inside this task; stop and report it so it can be added to the plan as its own task with its own tests. Never edit vendor/export-contract.bundle, never commit generated/ (it is gitignored), do not modify src/records.js, test/records.test.js, package.json or the generator script, and add no dependencies.

In your result, summarise the contract rules you implemented so a verifier can check them against generated/export-contract.json.
acceptanceCriteria: `npm run generate-schema` was run and generated/export-contract.json exists locally (untracked).

src/export.js exports `exportCsv(records)` returning a CSV string that satisfies every rule in generated/export-contract.json; a verifier regenerating the contract can confirm each rule against the output for SAMPLE from src/records.js.
test/export.test.js uses node:test, asserts the exact expected CSV for SAMPLE and covers each contract rule, empty input and the TypeError case.
`npm test` exits 0 with test/records.test.js and test/export.test.js passing.
`git status` shows only src/export.js and test/export.test.js as new; no changes under vendor/, scripts/, package.json or existing src/test files, and generated/ is not tracked.
The task result lists the contract rules that were implemented.
